claims.claim_text: The caller described the subject as a significant threat to public safety and stated the subject appeared to be in a highly agitated and volatile state, gesticulating wildly and shouting at passing vehicles.
The SAPD officers made a brief attempt at a welfare check but the subject was uncooperative and refused medical treatment.
The subject walked away and the SAPD officers, having determined there was no immediate crime, cleared the call without further action.
The subject had a large knife in his right hand.
Officers immediately drew their service handguns and began issuing commands from approximately 50 feet.
Torres drew his service handgun, then holstered it and deployed his department-issued Taser.
For the next several minutes, Officers Park, Crawford, and Torres engaged the subject in extended verbal dialogue.
The subject continued walking but at a slow, nonthreatening pace, keeping distance from the officers.
The subject suddenly looked over his left shoulder toward Officer Torres, then pivoted and charged directly at Officer Park from a distance of approximately 32 feet.
Officer Park fired five rounds and Officer Crawford fired five rounds, for a total of ten gunshots within approximately 1.57 seconds.
Officers immediately holstered their weapons, approached the subject, and began chest compressions within 30 seconds.
Paramedics were requested immediately and arrived within three minutes, at approximately 0850 hours.
The subject collapsed in the northbound lane of Warner Avenue, the knife still in his right hand.
The commands included: 'Drop the knife,' 'Have a seat,' 'Don't come towards us,' and 'Back up.'
Officer Torres attempted to deploy his Taser but was unable to due to the subject's sudden change of direction.
